title: Stress-Testing Efficient Responsible-AI Evaluation: When Compute Savings Change Benchmark Conclusions
reason: The paper focuses on how computational efficiency interventions (such as quantization, batching, and subsetting) affect the measurement conclusions of responsible-AI benchmarks. While the benchmarks used (BBQ and BBQ-V) include 'Religion' as one of several demographic categories to test for social bias, the paper's core research question is about evaluation robustness and methodology, not the study of faith, ethics, or moral reasoning.
